text.p: Costilla Energy Inc sees production rising to about 5 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe) this year, President Mike Grella said on Friday.

The company produced 2.2 million boe of oil and natural gas in the first half of the year as gas production nearly doubled to 6,721 million cubic feet (mmcf) from 3,504 mmcf in the same period last year.
"I expect we'll produce prior to the acquisition at 5 million barrels," Grella said, excluding production from the company's pending acquisition of Ballard Petroleum LLC.

Costilla on Thursday reported a $2.4 million or $0.23 a share second quarter net loss compared to a $2.3 million or $0.44 a share loss including a one-time $1.6 million charge in the comparable period last year.
The Midland, Texas-based company's second quarter 1997 net loss was fueled by sharply higher production, exploration and dry hole costs and weaker oil and gas prices.
Prices fell below $17.50 a barrel in the second quarter, but have since rebounded to about $18.25 a barrel equivalent in August, he said.
